title: Joining Eckford's band on Beale Street
summary: In Memphis he sat in on a split-drum job, impressed with his bells, joined Eckford's band, and shared the Metropolitan Theater with drummer Baker.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Can you tell us the next band you joined, or show, whatever it was?

Well, the next band, I... We went into Memphis. We went back for a little vacation, a couple of weeks. And while I was in Memphis, I went up on Beale Street, and I saw a sign in a nightclub like this, stuff snare drum was split. He couldn't use it. And so he was, didn't know what to do and I stepped up and gave him my card with my name on it. I was very proud of that card, Jasper Taylor, drums, bells, xylophone and Dandy Dixie Minstrels. And he said, well where is your drum? I told him it was on the car at the station. This was a railroad show. We had two cars, a baggage car and a car for sleeping. So we made a deal and I went down and got my drum and brought it back up. And so he played a few pieces and I, on the inside of me, told me that I could, was a better drummer than this young man. And it wasn't long before he extended me an invitation to play a tune. And this tune that they played was a tune that the musical band was playing. And I was right at home and then he got out the drum parts to, had bells, a lot of bells, a lot of bell work. And he wanted to see if I could play the bells as I stated on my business card.
And so they were very well pleased.
What was the name of that band again?
Did you meet Handy up there in Memphis soon?

Well, the news seemed to spread all over. The next day the boys made me very welcome and told me to go get my clothes and leave the musical show. They were going to get me with a band. And this drummer was drumming in the Metropolitan Theater and carrying me. His name was Mr. Baker. And I'll never forget him. And so he he split his work with me. He let me play in the theater and I played the shows. And I knew show business because I was playing a big menstrual show that had bottom legs.
About what year was that? Can you remember?
